answer: When k bonded identities equivocate in a coordinated pattern, each identity’s penalty rises with the number of corroborating pairs, producing O(k²) aggregate slashing rather than a per-account fee. Detection seizes escrow and applies asymmetric depreciation to remaining capital, so a sybil swarm faces an exponential multiplier in capital loss. The shale ledger records evidence; hollow identities gain no protection, even when deployed as a comet burst.
